page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance in the Enhanced family, driven by a KVM hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with two threads per core, clocked at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA. The instance is allocated 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It operates with no bundled local storage, requiring external block storage, and includes a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate multi-threaded capacity contrasted with constrained single-core throughput. While Geekbench single-core (951.0) and stress-ng single-core tests place in the lower quartile, multi-threaded workloads exhibit standard throughput, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 23,344.34 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 23,406.46. Memory-intensive benchmarks show mixed results: uncached large-block read bandwidth reaches 119.7 GB/sec, yet overall PassMark memory performance remains in the lower quartile at 1,798.36. In-memory data store operations handle 23.48 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput achieves 14.04 GB/sec.

Given its balance of 32 vCPUs, 128.0 GB memory, and 15 Gbps networking, the instance offers practical resource density for parallel tasks that do not depend on high single-threaded clock speed. Because it lacks onboard NVMe storage, I/O performance relies on detached block volumes. The ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is technically matched for distributed web serving tiers, software compilation pipelines, container clusters, and intermediate relational or key-value database engines.

Built on x86_64 architecture with 16 physical cores and AVX-512 support, it maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The configuration provides 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local instance storage, requiring network-attached block volumes. Benchmark testing shows average multi-core execution alongside weaker single-threaded performance, as seen in Geekbench and compression metrics. Redis SET throughput measures 23.48 million operations per second, with static web serving reaching 14.04 GB/sec. The instance delivers steady capacity for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, web fleets, microservice orchestrators, and caching tiers.
